extracted.intended_audience: Navy officials, government contracting analysts, contract managers, and scholars studying privatization/OMB A-76 implementation
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation of the U.S. Navy's post-award costs and implementation issues arising from contracting out under OMB Circular A-76, focusing on food service and storage/warehousing operations under multi-function contracts. The study identifies costs underestimated or omitted from pre-award cost comparisons and recommends policy, accounting, and administration changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of pre-award cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: The accuracy of pre-award cost estimates for estimating post-award program savings in operations that are contracted out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commercial Activities program (OMB Circular A-76) has been controversial largely because pre-award estimates may not accurately predict post-award results. The thesis examines whether pre-award cost comparisons properly estimate the savings realized after contracting out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of underestimated or unaccounted post-award costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifies those costs that are either underestimated or not accounted for in the cost comparison process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research on 14 West Coast activities contracting out food service and/or storage and warehousing found categories of post-award costs missing or undervalued in pre-award analyses; evaluations should explicitly look for such omitted or underestimated cost elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award guidance and policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The need for post-award guidance and policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective implementation requires formal post-award guidance and policy to govern how contracted operations are managed and how savings are validated after contract award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claimant guidance at the field level
rubrics_metrics.description: The need for increased claimant guidance at the field level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field-level claimants (actors responsible for implementing or overseeing contracts) require clearer instructions and support to ensure consistent application of A-76 processes and accurate reporting of post-award costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate cost accounting system and post-award program controls
rubrics_metrics.description: The absence of an adequate cost accounting system and post-award program controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robust cost accounting and control mechanisms are necessary to track actual costs after award; without them, comparisons between in-house and contractor costs are unreliable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract administration staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: The need for increased contract administration staffing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sufficient contract administration personnel are required to manage contracted operations, monitor contractor performance, and validate cost savings over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget flexibility at activities that have contracted out
rubrics_metrics.description: A problem with budget flexibility at activities that have contracted out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting out can create budgetary constraints or inflexibilities at activities; evaluations should assess how budget structure and flexibility affect post-award operations and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance definition clarity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poorly defined performance requirements make it difficult to compare contractor and in-house performance and to assess whether contracted services meet expectations; clear performance definitions are a necessary evaluation criterion.
